subject.title: [Bug]: Discord sessions persist per-session exec directives, causing allowlist mode to behave unexpectedly after config changes

question: Should persisted per-session `/exec` defaults continue to override later global or agent exec config, or must operator config changes invalidate or dominate stored session exec fields?
rationale: Current code, docs, and tests treat `/exec` as persistent session state, but the report shows that this can conflict with administrator security policy changes; the permanent precedence and migration behavior is a security/product contract choice.

options.title: Operator config wins
options.body: Make later global or agent exec policy dominate or invalidate stored session exec fields, with migration or reset handling for existing persisted entries.

options.title: Keep session defaults
options.body: Keep current per-session precedence and document an explicit operator reset path for sessions that should pick up stricter config.

options.title: Add reset/versioning
options.body: Preserve per-session overrides until the underlying exec policy fingerprint changes, then clear or revalidate the stored exec fields.

recommendation.title: Operator config wins
recommendation.body: Make later global or agent exec policy dominate or invalidate stored session exec fields, with migration or reset handling for existing persisted entries.

likelyOwner.reason: The relevant behavior and focused resolver tests trace back most directly to the `/exec` session override work and follow-up coverage.
